title: Your Brain Treats Future You Like a Total Stranger

scenes.text: Your brain thinks the future you is a complete stranger.
Researchers put people in a brain scanner and asked them to think about themselves today, then ten years from now.
Thinking about your future self lit up the brain in a different pattern. One that looked a lot like thinking about some other person.
That's why saving, exercising and studying feel so hard. You're being asked to sacrifice for someone your brain barely knows.
So the team showed people an aged photo of their own face. Afterwards, those people put far more money aside for the future.
Want to make a better choice today? Picture yourself at eighty, and ask what they'd want. What would your future self tell you right now?

description:
Your brain treats your future self like a stranger.
In brain-scan studies led by psychologist Hal Hershfield, thinking about yourself ten years from now produced activity patterns closer to thinking about another person than about your present self. That is part of why saving and other long-term choices feel like sacrifices.
When people were shown an aged image of their own face, they set aside far more money for the future.
What would your future self tell you to do today?
